official.deadline_note: Third-party nomination window runs 15 September to 30 November, ahead of the 1 December application deadline. Renewal requires applying for financial aid annually by 15 March.
official.application_cycle: Annual fall-entry cycle; nominations 15 September-30 November with the first-year application due 1 December
official.status_note: The University states nominations open 15 September and close 30 November, and that the first-year application should be submitted by 1 December for priority scholarship consideration.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The Handler Scholarship (combined with any federal and state grants/scholarships) will cover your tuition and mandatory fees for up to eight semesters or until your first bachelor degree requirements are met, whichever comes first.
benefits: A more-than-full-tuition, four-year scholarship to the University of Rochester
A four-year scholarship in the amount of the cost of attendance; health insurance is covered if applicable
Enrichment fund of up to $5,000 to support other enhancements or needs related to the academic experience
Academic Supply grant of $100 per year to purchase supplies needed for class at the University bookstore
Access to a special alumni network made up of past Handler Scholars
Eligibility to pursue additional funding through the RIG, REACH and/or Discover programs for summer internships and undergraduate research
eligibility: First-year, fall term domestic and international applicants (transfer and spring applicants are not eligible)
Resiliency in the face of complex challenges
High financial need as demonstrated on the CSS Profile and FAFSA
Nomination by a high school or independent counselor, teacher, or community-based organization official; nominations are not accepted from students or parents
requirements: Submit the University of Rochester first-year application; it does not have to be Early Decision but should be submitted by December 1
Complete the FAFSA and CSS Profile so financial need can be assessed (FAFSA school code 002894, CSS Profile school code 2928)
Be nominated by an eligible third party during the 15 September to 30 November window
Maintain Satisfactory Academic Progress (SAP) as defined by the University and Federal SAP Policy to renew the scholarship
Apply for financial aid annually by March 15 for full consideration
Notify the dedicated Handler Financial Aid counselor of any required course-related fees so awards can be adjusted
International applicants must submit English proficiency exam results or a waiver request by their application deadline
documents: University of Rochester first-year admission application (Common Application or Coalition/Scoir)
Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA), school code 002894
Third-party nomination submitted by a counselor, teacher, or community-based organization official between 15 September and 30 November
Secondary school transcript and school report/counselor recommendation
Teacher recommendation (one required) and mid-year report (when available)
English language exam results (DET, IELTS, or TOEFL iBT) or an English Proficiency Waiver Request for international applicants
selection_criteria: Outstanding potential to be future leaders
Substantial financial need as demonstrated on the CSS Profile and FAFSA
coverage: Tuition and mandatory fees for up to eight semesters or until the first bachelor degree requirements are met, whichever comes first
Housing and food, on campus based on housing and meal plan selection or off campus via a standard allowance for rent, utilities, groceries, and transportation to campus
Books and supplies through a $100 per year Academic Supply grant at the University bookstore
Personal and transportation expenses via an annual allowance in the cost of attendance, with travel based on distance from hometown to campus
application_method: Submit the University of Rochester first-year application (Common Application or Coalition) by December 1; Early Decision is not required and Regular Decision by December 1 is not binding
Complete the FAFSA and CSS Profile by December 1 so need can be determined
Arrange for a high school or independent counselor, teacher, or community-based organization official to submit a nomination between 15 September and 30 November; students and parents cannot nominate
Finalists attend a mandatory two-part virtual interview event in mid-February; recipients may be invited to visit River Campus in late spring
official.application_route: No separate scholarship application: all first-year applicants are reviewed automatically by submitting the URochester application plus FAFSA and CSS Profile by December 1, with a third-party nomination filed between September 15 and November 30
official.citizenship_residency: No citizenship restriction is published; first-year fall-term applicants may be domestic or international
official.international_eligibility: Yes. The University states international students are eligible and will be selected each year, and Handler Scholars are representative of the overall class
official.duration: Four years, the duration of the regular four-year academic program; tuition and mandatory fees covered for up to eight semesters or until the first bachelor degree requirements are met, whichever comes first
official.description: Established in 2007 by Rich and Martha Handler with an ultimate commitment of $25 million, the largest scholarship gift in the University's history, the Alan and Jane Handler Scholarship is the University of Rochester's premier award. It provides assured, complete financial support (tuition, fees, housing, food, books, personal expenses and transportation) plus individual and group opportunities for the duration of the regular four-year academic program.
official.region: North America (Rochester, New York, United States)
official.program_type: Need-based full-cost-of-attendance undergraduate scholarship; the University's premier award
official.english_requirement: International applicants whose native language is not English and who attend secondary school in a non-English-speaking country must submit DET 130, IELTS 7.5, or TOEFL iBT 100 (former scoring) / 5 (new scoring); a waiver is available for native English speakers or those who completed at least three years of high school in English. Scores or a waiver request are due by the application deadline

verification.notes: Checked the Handler Scholarship page, the Dates & Deadlines page, the International Students page, and the Financial Aid page on rochester.edu. The award is published only as the cost of attendance with no fixed dollar figure (the $5,000 enrichment fund and $100 per year supply grant are the only published component amounts), so no numeric amount was recorded; full-time enrolment is not stated on the Handler page.

applicant_utility.summary: There is no separate Handler application: every first-year applicant who files the URochester application plus FAFSA and CSS Profile by 1 December is reviewed automatically, so the real gating step is securing a nomination from a counselor, teacher, or community organization official during the 15 September to 30 November window, because the University refuses nominations from students and parents. Plan around the mid-February two-part virtual interview, which is mandatory for finalists and hard to reschedule. Note that the award is need-based, so a strong transcript alone will not carry it: the CSS Profile and FAFSA must show substantial need. Recipients keep the award by maintaining Satisfactory Academic Progress and re-filing for aid by 15 March each year.
applicant_utility.best_fit: First-year fall-entry applicants, domestic or international, with an outstanding academic record, a documented history of overcoming significant obstacles, high financial need, and a counselor or teacher willing to nominate them by 30 November.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm a nominator (high school or independent counselor, teacher, or community-based organization official) in September; the window closes 30 November and self- or parent-nominations are rejected

File the FAFSA (code 002894) and CSS Profile (code 2928) by 1 December; both are needed for need to be assessed, so plan for the CSS fee or request the fee waiver (first-year international deadline 15 January) early

Decide between Early Decision and Regular Decision deliberately: the Handler review does not require binding ED, and a Regular Decision application filed by 1 December still gets priority scholarship consideration and a late-February decision

Ask your school to send the transcript, school report, counselor recommendation, and mid-year report through Common App or Coalition/Scoir directly, and book any required English test early enough for official scores to arrive before the deadline
Block the calendar for a mandatory two-part virtual interview in mid-February and tell the Handler team immediately if a genuine conflict arises
common_rejection_risks: No nomination on file because the student assumed the application alone was enough or tried to self-nominate, which the University does not accept
Missing the 1 December deadline, which removes the applicant from priority scholarship review entirely
FAFSA or CSS Profile left incomplete so substantial financial need cannot be demonstrated, or IDOC follow-up documents never sent to the College Board
Applying as a transfer or spring-entry student, both of which are ineligible for this scholarship
Missing the mandatory mid-February finalist interview without prior communication, since participation is a required part of the process
International applicants submitting English scores or the waiver request after the application deadline, leaving the admission file incomplete
Renewal lost through dropping below Satisfactory Academic Progress or missing the 15 March annual aid application
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The scholarship does not cover Rocky Bucks/Flex Account spending, non-required individual fees such as dorm damage, parking tickets, library charges, and Dean's fees. The off-campus housing and personal/transportation allowances are capped at reasonable local costs and travel is based on hometown distance, so students living off campus above the allowance or taking extra trips home pay the difference themselves. Unused $100 book grants are not refundable or transferable.
document_audit: Nominators receive a submission confirmation and every nominee gets an email with next steps; if nothing arrives within a few days, the nominator must contact the admissions office before the window closes
The CSS Profile must go to school code 2928 and the FAFSA to 002894; a profile filed to the wrong school leaves the need analysis unprocessed
Required documents must come from the school, testing agency, or family directly through Common App or Coalition/Scoir; URochester will not process documents emailed in by another third party
Handler students must proactively notify their dedicated Handler financial aid counselor of required course-related fees or the award will not be adjusted to cover them
Enrichment fund requests must be submitted before the last date of the term in which the expense falls, so retroactive summer or study-abroad spending is not reimbursable
alerts: The nomination deadline (30 November) falls one day before the application deadline (1 December), so the nominator has to act before the applicant finishes the file

The interview event in mid-February is mandatory even though admission decisions for priority applicants are not released until late February, so a finalist wait can fall inside a busy decisions month
The scholarship is need-based and selective: nomination does not guarantee acceptance or the award, though finalists who miss out remain eligible for other high-value and merit scholarships
Aid renewal is conditional: keep Satisfactory Academic Progress and reapply for financial aid by 15 March every year, and remember enrichment requests must precede the last day of the relevant term
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Counselor or teacher files the nomination by 30 November, the student submits the application with FAFSA and CSS Profile by 1 December, finalists are emailed in mid-February for the mandatory virtual interview, and the award letter arrives with the financial aid package shortly after admission.
